subject: Post-demo: token profile, unit-econ target & approval path
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cooper <ethan.cooper@atlasai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: token profile, unit-econ target & approval path

Hi Ethan — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and three asks so we can size a sensible proposal: 

Recap (2 bullets):
- You’re planning to ship the summarization + retrieval pipeline in Q4; initial internal beta for a subset of users in 6–8 weeks.
- Expected steady-state usage is mainly summaries (short responses) with occasional long-generation bursts for batch reports.

Asks (can you confirm by EOD Wednesday?):
1) Range for expected monthly token consumption (best guess is fine). If you can give low/typical/high that helps our cost modeling.
2) Target unit economics — i.e., target $/1M tokens you’d expect us to aim for (or current internal benchmark).
3) Who is the economic buyer and who will actually sign the PO/contract on the finance side? If you want, drop the name + email for procurement.

Attachments: I’ve attached a high-level pricing estimate and a proposed mutual action plan so you can see how we land on commit vs. on-demand.

Proposed next steps: once we have the three items above we’ll:
- Put together a 2-option pricing band (on-demand + 6-month reserved)
- Prep a short SOW/PO-ready summary for procurement and legal
- Schedule a 30-min procurement intro if needed

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cooper <ethan.cooper@atlasai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Malik <sana.malik@atlasai.com>, procurement@atlasai.com
Date: 2026-07-15T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: token profile, unit-econ target & approval path

Rafael — great recap, appreciate the succinct write-up. Answers below: 

1) Monthly token ranges (estimates):
- Low (pilot): 4–6M tokens/month
- Typical (post-beta): 15–22M tokens/month
- Peak (launch spikes + batch reports): up to ~40M tokens in heavy months

2) Target unit economics: we’re looking to keep infra spend for generation under ~$700/1M tokens as an internal target; if we can get to ~$650 that’s ideal. We don’t have a fixed public benchmark — this is internal guidance from product finance.

3) Approval path / contacts:
- Economic buyer: Sana Malik (Head of Data Products) — sana.malik@atlasai.com (cc’d)
- Finance/procurement contact who will sign: procurement@atlasai.com (generic address)
- Engineering approval (technical SOW): Chris Yang, VP Engineering (chris.yang@atlasai.com) — he’ll need a short SOW and an ops checklist.

Other asks:
- Can you send SOC 2 + data retention and deletion policy? Procurement will want those.
- If you have a sample SOW we can review that speeds things up.

Timeline: aiming to finalize procurement by end of quarter (Aug 31) if possible.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cooper | Director, Product 
AtlasAI

Forwarding Ethan’s reply — key items: 15–22M typical / peaks to 40M, target ~$650–700 per 1M, economic buyer is Sana, procurement@general for signature, Chris Yang needs SOW.

Monica/Marissa — can you: 
- Confirm whether $650–700 puts them in the mid-tier discount band (and what a 6-month reserved commit would look like)?
- Prep SOC2 + data-retention doc to send to procurement.
- Draft a short SOW template we can push to Chris for engineering sign-off (1–2 pages).

I’ve attached the pricing estimate and the MAP for reference. If we want to be proactive I can propose the procurement intro slot next week (Mon/Tue windows).

Thanks — Rafael

Thanks Rafael — quick notes from pricing/procurement side: 

- Banding: $650–700/1M sits with our standard reserved-commit discount. For ~15–22M/mo we’d propose two options:
  • On-demand: $800/1M
  • 6-month reserved (committed billing): $700/1M + ability to burst; or
  • 6-month reserved with 12% commit discount (if they commit to a higher floor) — effective ~$616/1M (show math in SOW)

- Next steps I’ll:
  1) Upload SOC 2 summary + data retention policy to the shared Drive (link below).
  2) Draft a 1–2 page SOW and attach initial-sow-draft.docx for review; Rafael / Ethan / Chris can iterate.
  3) I can run the pricing scenarios in the deal calculator and share an ROI slide for Ethan’s finance team.

Ethan — if you can confirm whether AtlasAI prefers a fixed-dollar PO or a recurring committed SKU, we’ll tailor the SOW language accordingly. Also, I’m happy to jump on a procurement intro — Tues 7/20 10:00am PDT or Wed 7/21 9:00am PDT work on our side.

Links/Attachments: initial-sow-draft.docx; https://drive.redwood.com/shared/atlasai/soc2-summary; https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1429

- Monica Patel | Pricing & Solutions | Redwood Inference
